independentReview.reason: TWO APPROVES and one REQUEST CHANGES at this exact head, and the disagreement was resolved on evidence rather than by orchestrator fiat. Reviewer A approved: head and base match, the anchor phrase survives at every commit so rules A and D are non-vacuous, rule C traced live across all 34 worktrees, doc-budget within cap with no cap moved, .githooks/ and scripts/ byte-identical to main, nothing under src/ or src-tauri/. Reviewer B requested changes on one defect: this PR replaces the stale lane name with its OWN branch name, so rule D fails again the instant this lands - proven with merge-tree rather than asserted. B characterized that as CHEAPLY AVOIDABLE, arguing the specific self-name could simply have been deleted because the following clause already states the general rule. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE, and was tested against the guard's source rather than argued: atRiskCarriers is carriers.filter(c => c.unpushed > 0) where unpushed is distance from every remote computed against trustedExclusions, which is the live git ls-remote set - so at pre-push time the commit being pushed is on no remote, the lane is at-risk, and rule C REQUIRES its name in the bullet. Bare deletion was not hypothetical: it is exactly what commit 5b1e3f9c did, and the gate refused it. The path-credit route does not escape either, because carriersMissingFromBullet credits a quoted path only when tail(span) === c.name.toLowerCase(), and for a branch carrier c.name is the branch while the worktree path tail is sentinel-land-312. Rather than overrule B, the orchestrator posted both verdicts and the refutation to the PR and dispatched a THIRD independent reviewer at the same unchanged head with both positions in hand, instructed to test each and to side with B if any concrete mechanism satisfied rule C at push time and left rule D green after merge. Reviewer C returned APPROVE with CATCH-22: REAL AND TOTAL, having read atRiskCarriers, carriersMissingFromBullet, liveCarriers and the countUnpushed wiring itself, and confirmed no local-only exemption path exists. C's judgement on the merge decision is recorded because it is the substantive one: landing is correct rather than merely tolerable, because holding the PR leaves main red on a claim about lane/rule-c-at-risk-312 that is now unconditionally false with no open PR fixing it, and a materially better fix exists only at the mechanism level - deriving rules A and D from live git state the way rule C already does, or exempting a lane that is an ancestor of origin/main at merge time - both of which are proposed in issue #333 and correctly left out of a narrowly scoped regression repair. DISCLOSED, NOT HIDDEN: merging this PR is EXPECTED to immediately re-fail rules A and D on main, on this PR's own branch name. That is the third reproduction of #333, it is stated in the PR body, in commit ecd79ee2's message, and in #333 itself, and the next lane should fix the mechanism rather than repeat the cleanup. One further disclosure about the review conduct: the orchestrator's first briefs were self-contradictory, banning file creation while demanding tests be run at a head only the writer's worktree had checked out. Reviewer A consequently reproduced the guards' git plumbing by hand instead of executing them, and created and deleted one scratch file outside any repo checkout. Reviewer A's pass is therefore a second independent derivation rather than a second gate execution; the gate execution at this head is the pre-push run recorded above. Brief three was corrected to permit reading blobs at the head and running existing scripts.
